Consult Summary:
- Teleconsult for new-onset, left-sided throbbing headache with photophobia for 1 day; no focal neurologic symptoms; clinician impression: likely migraine; advised NSAID plus acetaminophen, hydration, safety-netting, BP check, and home thermometer.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Severe headache for ~1 day.
- Onset/timing: Began yesterday morning on waking.
- Location/character: Left-sided, throbbing; intensity fluctuates (never fully resolves).
- Exacerbating/relieving factors: Worse with light/sunlight; improved by lying down. Not worse with lying flat, bending forward, coughing, or sneezing.
- Associated symptoms: Photophobia. Denies visual disturbances, abnormal smells/tastes, nausea, vomiting, fever (no temperature measured), upper respiratory symptoms, weakness/tingling/numbness, or skin changes/rash.
- Intake: Eating and drinking normally.
- Baseline headaches: No prior history of regular headaches or migraines.
- Gynecologic: Not linked to menstrual cycle; last period ~1 week ago.
- Functional impact: Stayed home; limited activity since onset.
- Recent triggers: Work-related stress possible; no other changes identified.

Past Medical History:
- No significant past medical problems reported.
- No recent hospital admissions or surgeries reported.

Medications:
- Microgynon (combined oral contraceptive pill) — dose/route/frequency not documented; started ~6 years ago; no notable side effects.
- Paracetamol (acetaminophen) taken for current headache — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Allergies: Aspirin — reaction: nausea (patient reports feeling very sick).

Social History:
- Living situation: Lives with housemates/friends.
- Alcohol: A few drinks on weekends.
- Tobacco: Does not smoke.
- Recreational drugs: Denies use.
- Occupational/psychosocial: Reports being stressed at work.

Family History:
- Mother: Hypertension; migraines.

Physical Examination:
- 

Investigations:
- Blood pressure reportedly checked ~6 months ago during repeat prescription; patient reports it has “always been fine.” No values provided.
- No labs or imaging obtained.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute unilateral throbbing headache with photophobia; new to patient — likely migraine per clinician impression; no red flags elicited in history.
  - Plan:
    - Trial NSAID (e.g., ibuprofen) along with acetaminophen (paracetamol) as advised; ensure adequate hydration. Doses not documented.
    - Safety net: Seek care promptly if headache worsens, changes in character, persists without improvement, fever develops, or rash appears.
    - If headaches become persistent, cyclical with menses, or have identifiable triggers, arrange follow-up for further evaluation/management.
- Issue 2: Combined oral contraceptive use (Microgynon) without recent BP documentation.
  - Plan:
    - Arrange blood pressure check (clinician advised).
- Issue 3: Reported aspirin intolerance (nausea).
  - Plan:
    - Avoid aspirin; patient has previously used other NSAIDs (e.g., ibuprofen/naproxen) in the past without recent use.

- General Plan items:
  - Obtain a home thermometer to monitor temperature as advised.

Quality checks:
● Missing expected elements:
  - No vital signs documented (including BP at this visit), no neurological exam documented.
  - Medication doses/route/frequency not documented.
  - Comprehensive allergy review beyond aspirin not documented.
  - Past surgical history not documented.
  - Pregnancy status not addressed.
● Internal conflicts:
  - None noted; patient denies eye/vision problems while reporting photophobia (not a conflict).
● Transcript quality:
  - Some segments were unclear or incomplete (personal details redacted/inaudible), but clinical content largely intelligible.
